caption: Paper-to-notebook correspondence and explicit claim boundaries under the real-data-only scope.
alt: Seven-row table mapping each paper component to its local implementation and supported claim boundary.
reading: Expected shortfall, joint risk confidence intervals and synthetic null-size/power Monte Carlo studies are intentionally omitted; empirical stability p-values are therefore reported as nominal paper-calibrated pivotal quantities.

caption: Full-sample GARCH(1,1)-t and GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t parameters, lag-1 absolute autocorrelation and local Bartlett HAC summaries across EUR, GBP and JPY.
alt: Nine-row diagnostic table reporting persistence, Student-t degrees of freedom, lag-1 absolute ACF, mean and minimum unfloored Bartlett HAC factors, and floor counts.
reading: All six volatility filters converged under both SLSQP initialization attempts with persistence between 0.9910 and 0.9991 and Student-t degrees of freedom between 5.35 and 8.83, sharply reducing lag-1 absolute autocorrelation while keeping finite-sample HAC factors visible.

caption: EUR/USD raw upper-loss tail path (n=6,769, m=200, h=0.10, J=20): Lambda_n=0.737, raw pivotal p=0.2430, Holm p=1.0000.
alt: Line plot of EUR/USD raw-loss local tail index from 2003 to 2021 with shaded 95 percent HAC uniform confidence band and dashed constant projection line.
reading: These two-sided retrospective estimates use observations before and after each date. The wide HAC band reflects local estimation variance and serial dependence; unclipped band endpoints are shown honestly.

caption: EUR/USD absolute standardized GARCH(1,1)-t innovations: Lambda_n=0.725, raw pivotal p=0.2521, Holm p=1.0000.
alt: Line plot of local tail-index estimates for EUR/USD GARCH absolute standardized residuals with shaded 95 percent HAC uniform band and dashed projection center.
reading: Filtering conditional variance shifts the target from raw one-sided currency losses to two-sided standardized shock magnitudes; a lower or smoother path estimates a distinct innovation tail rather than 'correcting' raw gamma.

caption: EUR/USD absolute standardized GJR-GARCH(1,1)-t innovations: Lambda_n=0.634, raw pivotal p=0.3305, Holm p=1.0000.
alt: Line plot of local tail-index estimates for EUR/USD GJR-GARCH absolute standardized residuals with shaded 95 percent HAC uniform band and dashed projection center.
reading: Allowing asymmetric variance responses to USD euro-holding losses leaves the standardized innovation tail path closely aligned with symmetric GARCH(1,1)-t on EUR/USD.

caption: Precision-weighted constant projection gamma_tilde, mean Bartlett HAC factor, omnibus statistic Lambda_n, raw pivotal p-value and nine-slot Holm-adjusted p-value (m=200, h=0.10, J=20).
alt: Nine-row table of baseline tail-stability tests across EUR, GBP and JPY for raw losses, GARCH innovations and GJR-GARCH innovations.
reading: All nine prespecified slots completed without filter failure. Decisions are nominal paper-calibrated pivotal outcomes at familywise alpha=0.05 (unscreened by synthetic dependent-null simulations); correlated USD exchange rates are not independent replications.

caption: Trailing 250-observation strict violation counts on EUR/USD (p=0.01, expanding window) across Arms A, B, C and D against the nominal 2.5 benchmark.
alt: Time-series line chart of rolling 250-day 1 percent VaR exceedance counts from 2009 to 2025 for static Arm A and dynamic Arms B, C and D.
reading: Leaving the 2008 crisis-era threshold frozen (Arm A) starves violations during quiet regimes, whereas updating the local threshold (Arms B, C and D) tracks regime shifts closely; violation counts alone do not rank forecast accuracy.

caption: Primary prediction contrast on EUR/USD (4,253 dates, p=0.01, expanding): mean daily loss(C)-loss(B) = -0.000224, paired L=20 block-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.000678, +0.000204].
alt: Chronological curve of cumulative daily pinball-loss differences between dynamic-shape Arm C and fixed-shape Arm B from 2009 through 2025.
reading: Primary verdict: inconclusive (95% block-bootstrap interval straddles zero). Downward movements mark periods where dynamic tail shape beat fixed 2008 shape; abrupt steps correspond to rare 1%-tail exceedance days where slope 0.99 magnifies quantile differences.

caption: Mean pinball loss, violation counts against nominal expectations, and asymptotic Kupiec unconditional-coverage and Christoffersen independence p-values on EUR/USD (4,253 origins).
alt: Eight-row score table comparing Arms A, B, C and D on EUR/USD at tail probabilities 0.01 and 0.025.
reading: Dynamic thresholding (Arm B vs Arm A) delivers the dominant reduction in pinball loss and restores realistic violation frequencies; differences among dynamic Arms B, C and D are an order of magnitude smaller.

caption: Mean daily pinball-loss difference loss(C)-loss(B) at p=0.01 across EUR, GBP, JPY and equal-weight common-date joint series for expanding and rolling-2,500 windows (scaled by 10^4).
alt: Horizontal interval plot showing Arm C minus Arm B mean pinball-loss differences and L=20 and L=60 moving-block bootstrap 95 percent intervals across eight currency-window combinations.
reading: Comparing expanding and rolling-2,500 windows alongside L=20 and L=60 block lengths exposes whether any incremental gain from updating gamma survives nonstationary history rules and wider dependence blocks.

caption: Pinball losses for Arms B, C and D and paired C-minus-B moving-block bootstrap intervals (L=20, 10, 60; 5,000 resamples) across EUR, GBP, JPY and the 4,253-date joint panel.
alt: Eight-row forecast comparison table for EUR, GBP, JPY and joint 3-FX across expanding and rolling-2,500 windows.
reading: All supporting series, window designs and block-length intervals are retained without cherry-picking; moving-block intervals remain approximate conditional summaries on correlated USD exchange rates.

caption: Baseline and six one-factor EUR/USD perturbations on [0.15, 0.85], each recalibrated with 5,000 independent Pareto draws; p-values are descriptive outside the 9-test Holm family.
alt: Seven-row robustness table showing recalibrated band cutoffs, Lambda_n statistics, descriptive p-values and HAC floor counts across raw, GARCH and GJR targets on EUR/USD.
reading: Changing m, h or J shifts finite-sample studentization and critical values noticeably—especially when J=30 approaches or exceeds mh—confirming why single-bandwidth curves must not be over-interpreted.

caption: Seven hashed 5,000-draw Pareto calibration caches (35,000 paths total) with 1,000-bootstrap 95% cutoff intervals; live run completed in 1.82s with 0 filter and 0 forecast failures.
alt: Seven-row table listing calibration configurations, short SHA-256 keys, band critical values c_0.95, omnibus critical values Lambda_0.95 and their 95 percent bootstrap intervals.
reading: With 5,000 pivotal draws per configuration, Monte Carlo uncertainty in c_0.95 and Lambda_0.95 is tight relative to empirical sampling noise; zero filter or forecast origins were dropped.
